# Contact

How to reach neon1, when, and what the first call covers.

Tell me what's on your mind, or ask for an opinion on how your operations run today.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Email** | [hello@neon1.tech](mailto:hello@neon1.tech) |
| **Call or text** | [(424) 32-neon1](tel:+14243263661), that's (424) 326-3661 |
| **Book a call** | [calendly.com/1isgladtobeofservice/neon1-consultation](https://calendly.com/1isgladtobeofservice/neon1-consultation) |
| **LinkedIn** | [Pradeep](https://www.linkedin.com/in/pradeep-tathineni/) and [neon1](https://www.linkedin.com/company/neon1llc) |
| **GitHub** | [neon1llc](https://github.com/neon1llc) |

## What to expect

- **Where:** remote from anywhere, or on site within about 30 miles of Queens, NY.
- **When:** weekends 8am to 8pm and weekday evenings, Eastern time.
- **Size:** a week or two up to six weeks, with at most two clients at a time.
- **First call:** free and 15 minutes. The main pain points and your options.
- **After:** a short proposal with options and estimates. Nothing starts until you pick one.

## Availability and urgent issues

Work happens in planned appointments on weekday evenings and weekends. There's no 24/7 or emergency response. If something can't wait, such as a security incident in progress, an outage your business can't run without, or fraud on an account, contact a provider who offers emergency coverage, and your bank or the service involved, first. Ongoing care after a project, and any response times that come with it, are agreed in writing before they start.

Please leave passwords, health details, and payment information out of any first message.

# The names

Where neon1, its slogan and its products get their names.

## neon1

The name nods to Neo from *The Matrix*, who brought peace between man and machine. Neo means new. Neon is unmissable. It's always written with a lowercase n.

## "1 is glad to be of service."

The slogan nods to Robin Williams' Andrew from *Bicentennial Man*, a machine who spends two centuries being of service while searching for his humanity. The 1 is me, Pradeep, neon1's sole owner and your dedicated deputy, and 1 is glad to be of service.

## The legal names

- **neon1 LLC**, a New York limited liability company, does business as **neon1**, a registered assumed name (see the [state registration](registration.md)).
- **N1 Supply LLC** does business as **N1 Supply**. It is an affiliate of neon1 LLC.

## Product names

Repositories that neon1 builds mainly for its own use carry the `neon1-` prefix, such as neon1-site and neon1-corpus. Products made for the public or for clients get names of their own, such as [Ready, Secure, Go](../products/ready-secure-go.md).

# How a project runs

Listen, propose, decide, build and hand over.

1. **Listen.** Show me how the work gets done today. One real example is enough.
2. **Propose.** Options from quickest fix to fuller build, each with an estimate, the effort, and the result.
3. **Decide.** You pick. Often it's a setting, a cleanup, or leaving it alone.
4. **Build.** Small changes, tested, and shown as they land.
5. **Hand over.** I check it does what we agreed, then show you and write it down, so you can run it without me. Ongoing care is optional.

Every project then runs through the same four layers in [1NEON](../products/1neon.md): Needs, Execute, Observe, Normalize. [See a sample project](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/example), with made-up data, or [try the demo](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/demo/).

# 1NEON help

Short answers about using the 1NEON client portal.

Short answers about using 1NEON. Signed in? Tap **?** at the top right of any page for help with that page.

## Getting started

### What is 1NEON?
The portal where we run your projects together, with what you need, the work, the results, and the handover in one place. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live).

### Can I try it first?
Yes, three ways, with no account. The [guided walkthrough](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live) plays a fictional project on the real portal in about three minutes (the full story takes about 13), with controls to pause, pick a chapter, or exit. The [interactive demo](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/demo/) is a working copy with made-up clients; your changes stay in your browser until **Start over**. The [sample project](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/example) is one made-up project to read, from request to handover. Short walkthroughs show one thing each: [joining from an invitation](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=invite), [adding a passkey](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=passkey), [adding an authenticator app](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=authenticator), and [texts and text codes](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=texts).

### How do I get in?
You need an invite. Open its link, enter your email, and sign in with an emailed code or a passkey. No password needed. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=invite).

### I didn't get the sign-in code.
Check spam or promotions, then wait a minute and choose **Send a new code**. Codes work for a few minutes, in the browser that asked. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=invite).

### Is there a tour?
Yes, offered at your first sign-in. Skip it or ask to be reminded, and replay it from **?** or your profile. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=invite).

## Projects and the four layers

### What are Needs, Execute, Observe, and Normalize?
The four layers every project moves through. **Needs** is what you want and the options to get there, **Execute** the work, **Observe** the results against the goals, and **Normalize** what makes it last: handover, training, and care. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live).

### What should I do first on a project?
Look at **Next step** at the top. It says what has to happen now and who it's waiting on, and moves on as soon as that's done. When nothing is waiting, it names the stage's goal and offers **Move to** the next stage. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=propose).

### What do Not assessed, On track, At risk, and Off track mean?
They're the project's health, someone's assessment of how it's going. A new project is **Not assessed** until the team sets it, on the overview or with a status update; starting work or moving stages doesn't change it. The overview shows who set it and when. Items have their own status: To do, In progress, Blocked, or Done. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=build).

### What if we rename, reorder, or hide stages?
Projects follow the new names and order. A hidden stage still shows while a project is in it, and under any name, Decide still asks for an approved option and Closed still ends a project.

### How do I tell you what I need?
On the project's **Needs** tab, tap **Add request** and finish a sentence with a few taps: what you'd like to do (or **+** for your own), what it's for, what happens now, how often, and when it's due. **Define another need** adds more, each its own request. Only the first choice is required. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=needs).

### Do I have to write a lot?
No. Each section shows what belongs there, an example, and one-tap suggestions. Discovery questions take a short answer where they're asked, and a real example helps most. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=start).

### How do I know when something changes?
The bell glows when something new happens, like an upload, a decision, or a stage change. Tap it to see what and who, and tap one to open it. Important changes also email you; choose which under **Notifications** in your profile. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=listen).

### How do I comment or change an item?
Tap its title. A panel opens with its status, owner, due date, details, and comments, which your whole organization sees. Options and measures open the same way. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=build).

### How do I check something off?
Tick the box beside it; counts on each tab show how many are done. A choice between options counts as one, done once one is approved, and a measure is done at its target. Status updates, decisions, and uploaded files don't count, but a **File needed** does, ticked when you send it. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=handover).

### How do I delete something?
Use the item's trash button or **Delete** in its panel; both ask first. Approved options and decisions can't be deleted, since they record what was agreed. Files can be deleted by their uploader and admins.

### What does the onion next to a project mean?
Progress. Needs is the center ring and Normalize the outside, each filling as its work gets done.

### What does the board show?
Every project as a card in its stage, from the first call to care after handover. Drag a card to move it, or use **Move to** on a phone. A closed project moves back the same way, or with **Reopen**. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=build).

### What does the timeline show?
Under **Projects**, **Timeline** draws each project from start to target date, colored by layer: the dashed line is today, the diamond the target, the lighter part time ahead, and red stripes time past the target. Each row says its stage and days left. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=care).

### How do I start a project?
Choose **New project** and answer a few questions; it starts with a fitting checklist you can change later. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=start).

### What is the calendar on Home?
A month at a time. The arrows step months, **Today** comes back, and the month list jumps from a year back to two ahead. Marks show due dates, milestones, project targets, and your organization's events; choose a day to see them. Editors add leave, closures, meetings, or care plan dates, for one day or several, timed or all day, repeating weekly or monthly. Below, **Overdue** and **Upcoming** start open and **Past** and **Repeated** folded, and leave in the next week shows under **Away this week**. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=calendar).

### What is Insights?
Charts from your organization's data: open and overdue work, on-time finishes, days to a decision, work finished per week, projects across the layers, and their health. Work counts as finished the day it was marked done (the latest, if reopened). The page explains each number. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=observe).

## Proposals, decisions, and signing

### What is a proposal revision?
neon1's options are issued together as a numbered proposal, such as 0039-r1, each option with its own ID, such as 0039-r1-B. Issuing freezes a copy, so what you approve is exactly what you read. Changed options come in the next revision (0039-r2), and earlier ones stay readable, marked as replaced. Each revision shows when its prices were checked; past the recheck date, approval waits for a refresh. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=propose).

### How do I approve an option?
On the **Needs** layer, compare the options and choose **Approve this option**. Add any conditions, such as "only after 6pm", then type your full name and tick the box; your typed name is your signature. The approval lists the option's terms again before you sign (its ID, description, price and whether it's fixed or an estimate, hours, rate, timeline, outside costs, and purchases) and records them exactly as shown, with your name and the time. To ask for a change, comment on the option or send a marked-up proposal. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=decide).

### Can I download the proposal?
Yes. **Read the proposal**, under the options, puts the discovery, goals, constraints, every option with what's in and out, how each price adds up, when you'd pay, purchases, what each of us will do, and the agreement on one page. **Print or save as PDF** keeps a copy, and **Download Word** gives one to mark up, each page carrying the number, such as 0039-r1. Approving in 1NEON counts the same as signing on paper. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=decide).

### How do I suggest changes to a proposal?
Comment on an option, or mark up the Word download and upload it to **Files**. 1NEON asks "Is this a revision of Proposal 0039-r1?"; choose **Yes** and it's filed beside that revision. neon1 answers with the next revision. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=decide).

### Who buys equipment or software for a project?
You do, in your organization's name, unless you agree neon1 does. Each option lists expected purchases with estimates, which appear under **Purchases** in Execute once you approve; mark each bought and **Attach the receipt**. neon1 buys only with the decision maker's signature or initials, and is paid back at cost, with the receipt. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=build).

### What if we need something new after approving?
Add it as a request. 1NEON asks whether it changes the agreed scope; if so, it waits for the next revision with its own price, so no work or cost is added without a written change. Anything else goes ahead as usual.

### Who can approve?
The project's named decision maker, or, if none, an admin of your organization. Only an admin can name or change the decision maker, under **People** on the overview, after confirming it's them, and each change is recorded. neon1 can't be named, since it proposes the options, except in its own organization. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=decide).

### Can I change my mind after approving an option?
Yes, until you accept the handover. The decision maker picks another option and presses **Choose this instead**, says why, and signs again. Before signing, the screen shows what the change replaces, what was already invoiced, the hours already logged, and the deposit asked now, if any. Nothing is billed twice: what was invoiced for the earlier option counts toward the new one, hours already worked count toward its hours, and if what you've paid comes to more than the new option can cost, the difference comes back as a credit at handover. The earlier decision isn't edited or deleted; it stays on record, marked replaced, with your reason on the new one. To go back to an option you replaced, neon1 confirms it in the next revision of the proposal, with today's prices, and you choose it again the same way. If the change needs work none of the options describe, ask neon1 for a new option. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=decide).

### What does approving an option commit us to?
An approval records that your organization agreed to that option as shown: its scope, cost, timeline, and any conditions. Both sides can rely on it, alongside your signed agreement with neon1, which governs the paid work.

### How do I accept a handover step?
On the **Normalize** layer, steps are ticked as they're done. Once all are, the decision maker chooses **Accept the handover**, notes what they checked if they like, and signs with their typed name. One signature accepts every step, each showing who accepted it and when. **Check it and accept** accepts one step early. Accepted steps can't be edited, and acceptance prompts the final invoice. Watch [the handover](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=handover) and [the final invoice](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=final).

### What do Cost, Quality, and Effort mean?
neon1's 1 to 5 assessment of each option, where more dots is always better. **Cost** is the total cost, **Quality** how fully it meets your requirements, and **Effort** your team's effort to adopt and run it. The written price is what you'd agree to, with one-time and recurring charges apart, and **How this adds up** shows the hours and when you'd pay. Demo and walkthrough figures are illustrative. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=propose).

## Files

### How do I send a file?
Use **Upload** next to a file I asked for, or upload in **Files** and pick its project. Tap a name to open it: PDFs, pictures, and text open in a tab, and anything else downloads. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=listen).

### Are files safe?
Every file is virus-checked before anyone can download it and stays private to your organization. Please don't upload passwords or keys.

### What can I upload?
Any kind of file, up to 100 MB each. Please don't upload passwords, keys, or other secrets, malware, or regulated data such as health or payment card details unless we have a written agreement that covers it.

## People and access

### What can viewers, editors, and admins do?
Viewers read and comment. Editors also add and change work. Admins also invite people and change access and settings. neon1 sets its own access, so People shows it without a way to change it. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=team).

### How do I invite someone?
Admins choose **Invite people** on **People**, and the person gets an email link. People shows whether each invitation went out; if not, or it got lost, choose **Resend**. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=team).

### Can 1NEON text me?
Once texts are on, yes. Add your mobile number on your profile, agree to texts, save, and type the code 1NEON texts you. Texts only say something new is waiting, with a link, never naming your organization, projects, or files. Reply STOP to turn them off. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=texts).

### Why does it ask me to confirm it's me?
Admin actions (inviting, changing access or settings, and deleting a project or someone else's comment or file) need a recent confirmation with a passkey, authenticator app, or text code, so a stolen email account isn't enough. Add any of them under Two-step verification on your profile; a second is a backup. Once confirmed, you won't be asked again for 12 hours in that sign-in. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=passkey).

### Can I use an authenticator app?
Yes. On your profile, choose **Set up** next to Authenticator app, scan the code with Google Authenticator, Microsoft Authenticator, 1Password, Authy, or similar, and type the 6-digit code it shows. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=authenticator).

### What's a passkey?
A sign-in with your face, fingerprint, or device PIN instead of a code. It's faster and phishing-resistant, since it only works on the real 1NEON site. Add one under Two-step verification on your profile, and 1NEON offers it first next time. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=passkey).

## Your account

### How do I change my name or the look?
Open your profile from the menu, change your name, title, theme, menu, or notifications, and choose **Save**. **Mini** keeps a slim menu of icons on the left. Two-step verification and signing out take effect at once. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=profile).

### How do I sign out?
Open your profile and choose **Sign out**.

### I lost my phone or my authenticator app.
You can still sign in with an emailed code; the second step is only for admin actions. If you have another method, confirm with it, then remove the lost one under Two-step verification and add a new one. If you've lost every method, email [hello@neon1.tech](mailto:hello@neon1.tech) from your account's address. Email alone isn't enough, since a stolen mailbox is what the second step guards against, so I first confirm who you are by calling a number already on record for you or your organization (never one from the email), plus another admin's written OK if your organization has one. Then I remove the lost methods, record it, and email you, and you add a new one. Meanwhile only admin actions wait. There's no self-service reset.

### My email address changed.
Your email is how 1NEON knows you, so it can't be changed on your profile. Ask an admin to invite the new address and deactivate the old one, or email [hello@neon1.tech](mailto:hello@neon1.tech). Earlier work stays under the old address.

### Who do I ask for access?
An admin of your organization. If you don't know who that is, or neon1's access needs to change, email [hello@neon1.tech](mailto:hello@neon1.tech).

## Invoices and paying

### Is a price fixed or an estimate?
The option says which, and **How this adds up** shows the work behind it. A fixed price is the whole price for the work described, changed only by a change you approve. An estimate is a range of hours at the option's hourly rate: you pay for hours worked, each listed as it's logged, never past the high end without your approval. Fewer hours cost less. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=decide).

### Where do I see the hours worked?
In **Hours**, under Execute. Each entry has its date, what it went to, and its length in quarter hours, under a bar showing hours against the estimate and their cost so far. Billed hours carry the invoice's number, and the invoice lists them, so the total can be checked. On a fixed price, hours are a record, not a bill. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=build).

### What if the work needs more hours than the estimate?
The high end is the most you pay for the approved work; hours past it are listed, not billed. If the work itself must change, neon1 says so before the high end and issues a revision with the new price, and nothing is added until you approve. If the work takes less than the deposit covered, neon1 refunds the difference as a credit.

### Where are invoices and payments?
In **Invoices**, under Execute, with what's paid and left on each. **Next step** links to one that's ready or overdue. Each opens on neon1's letterhead with its number, lines, due date, and how to pay, ready to print or save as a PDF. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=pay).

### How do I pay an invoice?
Choose **Pay**. Stripe's secure page opens for bank transfer (ACH, preferred) or card, and 1NEON never sees your details. A card shows as paid within a minute. A bank transfer shows as started that day and paid once it clears, usually in a few business days, with **Pay** gone meanwhile. Check, Zelle, or wire work too, with the invoice number in the memo, and neon1 records them on arrival. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=pay).

### What if my bank payment doesn't go through?
No money moved. The invoice reopens with the failed payment listed, 1NEON tells you and neon1 that day, and **Next step** and **Needs you** point to it. Choose **Pay again** or another way to pay. Nothing is added to what you owe.

### Do I get a receipt?
The invoice is your receipt. Once paid it reads **Paid in full**, with each payment's date, amount, and method, and prints or saves as a PDF. Billing contacts are also emailed when a payment arrives.

### Is there a fee for paying by card, or for paying late?
No. The total is what you pay, however you pay, with no card surcharge, late fee, or interest. A late invoice shows as overdue, and neon1 may pause work, after telling you, once one is more than 30 days overdue.

### What if I think an invoice is wrong?
Say so before you pay: email [hello@neon1.tech](mailto:hello@neon1.tech) with the invoice number and line. Invoices for hours list every entry, so you can point to one. An issued invoice is never edited; neon1 fixes it with a credit, or voids it with a reason and issues a new one, on the record.

### When are invoices sent?
As your option's **When you pay** says. A deposit, half a fixed price or half an estimate's low end, comes at approval, and the rest at handover acceptance: the remainder of a fixed price, or the hours worked less the deposit, listed. Purchases are billed at cost with the receipt, and care plans monthly. Invoices are due in 15 days unless the option says otherwise, and each emails your billing contacts. Watch [the deposit](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=pay) and [the final invoice](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=final).

### Can an invoice be changed?
Not once issued; it's kept exactly as issued. A mistake is fixed with a credit, or by voiding it with a reason, both on record. An invoice with a payment, or one clearing, can't be voided.

### What is the service agreement?
neon1's terms for all work with your organization: how work is agreed, paying, ownership, confidentiality, and ending it. An admin signs it once in 1NEON, from **Settings**, before the first approval, and it covers every project. Read it any time at [/1NEON/agreement](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/agreement). [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=decide).

## Support and your data

### Something urgent is wrong. Who do I tell?
Email [hello@neon1.tech](mailto:hello@neon1.tech) with what happened and when. neon1 works planned hours with no emergency response, so for something that can't wait, such as bank fraud or an outage, contact the provider responsible first. Report a security problem in the portal itself to [security@neon1.tech](mailto:security@neon1.tech).

### Can we get a copy of our data?
Yes. There's no export button, so ask at [hello@neon1.tech](mailto:hello@neon1.tech) and I'll send your organization's data in a common format.

### What happens to our data when the work ends?
It's kept as the record of our work, for either of us to refer back to, unless your organization asks me to delete it. You can stop using 1NEON any time, and ask for an export first. The [privacy policy](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/privacy) has the details, including how long backups and audit records last.

### Who can I contact?
Email [hello@neon1.tech](mailto:hello@neon1.tech).

# Working with neon1

Short answers on where, when, how long, how much, and how data is handled.

## Do you come on site?

Yes, within about 30 miles of Queens, NY. I also work remotely, or on your own network through a secure connection that I set up for the job and that's removed when it's done.

## When do you work?

Saturdays and Sundays from 8am to 8pm, and weekday evenings from 6pm (until 9pm Monday to Thursday, 8pm on Friday), Eastern time, typically with 10 to 20 hours a week for project work. The booking calendar shows what's open.

## What if something urgent comes up?

I work in planned appointments on weekday evenings and weekends, with no 24/7 or emergency response. A security incident in progress or an outage you can't run without needs a provider with emergency coverage. Ongoing care, and any response times, are agreed in writing. Email [hello@neon1.tech](mailto:hello@neon1.tech) for anything else.

## How long does a project take?

Small jobs take a week or two, medium ones two to four weeks, and bigger projects four to six. I take on up to two clients at a time so each one gets proper attention.

## How is the cost worked out?

After the first call I send a short proposal with options, usually a quick fix, a solid setup, and a fuller build. Each gives a cost estimate, what it covers, the effort, the upkeep, and how it copes with failure. Every option meets the same security and quality baseline; a smaller one does less, not worse. You pick. If the scope changes, I'll tell you before the cost does. [See how options look in 1NEON](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=propose).

## How do you treat our data and accounts?

Before any paid work, we sign a short [service agreement](../policies/service-agreement.md) once, in 1NEON or on paper. It covers your systems and information: only the access the job needs, kept confidential, and removed when we're done. Each project is then a [proposal](../examples/proposal-options.md) with options, and choosing one, signed on paper or in 1NEON, is what we both agree to, including what I need from you. Work with personal or health data needs the right agreement first, such as a Business Associate Agreement. [See a handover in 1NEON](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=handover).

## How do I pay?

Invoices come through [1NEON](../products/1neon.md), in the project they belong to, and are due within 15 days. Each option in a proposal is priced one of two ways, and says which: a fixed price for work that's well understood, or an estimate, which is billed for the hours I work, lists each one, and never passes its high end unless you approve a change first. A project usually starts with a deposit (half of a fixed price, or half of an estimate's low end), and the rest is billed once you accept the handover. You can pay online by bank transfer (ACH) or card through Stripe, or by check, Zelle, or wire. There's no surcharge for any of them. If I buy equipment or software for you, you pay back exactly what the receipt shows, with no markup.

## Do you run security training?

Yes, for groups from parents and teachers to engineers and executives. Sessions cover phishing, fraud, data brokers, passwords, networks, cameras, smart devices, and physical security. For organizations I add privacy policies, data handling, security frameworks, and incident response.

## What don't you do?

I don't repair electronics, though I debug software and hardware installs and get them working together. I don't handle personal or health data without the right agreements, such as a Business Associate Agreement, but I can help you get them. I'm not a lawyer, but I'll work with yours on the technical side.

# 1NEON

The neon1 client portal that comes with a client engagement, where each project runs from the first call to handover.

The neon1 client portal at [neon1.tech/1NEON](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/). Each project runs through four layers: Needs, Execute, Observe, and Normalize. Proposals, signed decisions, files, invoices, and results stay together from the first call to handover.

- **Available now,** as part of working with neon1. It comes with a client engagement and isn't sold on its own.
- **Who it helps:** the people at a client organization who follow a project, send files, and approve options, and the administrators who decide who can see what.
- **For example,** I issue a proposal with two options for a project, numbered 0039-r1. The person named as decision maker compares them and signs their approval of 0039-r1-B with a typed name, and 1NEON keeps their signature, the time, and a copy of the option's terms as they saw them. The deposit invoice follows in the same project, and they can pay it by bank transfer or card.

## Current limits

- Access is by invitation only, from neon1 or an administrator of your organization.
- Online payments go through Stripe Checkout, by bank transfer (ACH) or card. Checks, Zelle, and wires are recorded by hand when they arrive.
- There's no export button. A copy of your organization's data is sent on request.
- Text messages work only once they're switched on and you've agreed to them on your profile.

## Next step

[See a sample project](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/example) or [try the demo](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/demo/), which runs in your browser with made-up data. To use 1NEON for real, start with [a first call](../company/contact.md). For help inside the portal, see [1NEON help](../faq/1neon-help.md).

Code: [neon1llc/neon1-1NEON](https://github.com/neon1llc/neon1-1NEON).

# Service agreement

neon1's service agreement, as a client organization signs it once in 1NEON: how work is agreed, purchases, paying, ownership, confidentiality, records, quality, limits, and ending.

**The short version**

- One agreement covers every project. Each option you approve sets that project's scope, price, and timeline.
- A price is fixed, or an estimate billed by the hour that never passes its high end without your approval. Invoices are due in 15 days.
- An admin signs once in 1NEON. Either of us can end it with 14 days' notice.

Edition 2.0

This agreement is between neon1 LLC, doing business as neon1 ("neon1", "I", "me"), and the organization named where it is signed in 1NEON ("you"). It covers every project I do for you while it is in effect.

## How work is agreed

Each project has a proposal in 1NEON, issued in numbered revisions. When your decision maker approves an option, its ID (for example 0039-r2-B) fixes that project's scope, price, and timeline. A change is agreed the same way, by approving an option in the next revision. This agreement governs everything else, and if a proposal and this agreement disagree, this agreement wins.

## Purchases

Prices for equipment, software, and services from other vendors are estimates. You buy them yourself, unless an approval says that I buy them for you. When I do, you pay me back exactly what I paid, shown by the receipt in 1NEON, with no markup.

## Paying

I send invoices through 1NEON. Each one is due within 15 days unless it says otherwise. An option's price is either fixed or an estimate, and the proposal says which. A fixed price is the whole price for the work described. An estimate is billed for the hours I work, at the rate it states; each hour is listed in 1NEON, and the total never passes the estimate's high end unless you approve a change first. An option may ask for a deposit when it is approved, as the proposal states. A deposit counts toward the final invoice; if the work done comes to less than a deposit you paid, I refund the difference. You can pay by bank transfer (ACH), card, check, Zelle, or wire. If an invoice is more than 30 days overdue, I may pause work until it is paid, after telling you.

## What you provide

You give me timely answers, the access the work needs, and accounts held in your organization's name. Please don't put passwords or other secrets in 1NEON.

## Ownership

Once you have paid for a project, what I made for you in it is yours. I keep my general know-how and the tools I had before or build for my own use, and open-source software stays under its own license.

## Confidentiality

We each keep what we learn about the other's business private, and use it only for the work. This doesn't cover what is already public or what the law requires us to disclose.

## Regulated data

I don't handle health records, payment card data, or similar regulated personal data unless we sign a separate agreement for it first, such as a business associate agreement.

## Records

I keep project records, signed approvals, invoices, and receipts, and I don't delete them on a schedule. If you ask me to delete something, I will, except what the law requires me to keep.

## Quality

I do the work with care. If something I delivered doesn't work as agreed and you tell me within 30 days of handover, I fix it at no charge.

## Limits

My total liability for any claim is limited to what you paid me for that project in the 12 months before the claim. Neither of us is liable to the other for indirect or consequential losses, such as lost profits.

## Ending

Either of us may end this agreement with 14 days' written notice, by message in 1NEON or by email. You pay for the work done and the purchases made up to that point.

## Signing and law

We agree to sign and keep these records electronically, and a name typed in 1NEON is a signature. You can ask me for a paper copy at any time. New York law governs this agreement.

# 1NEON guide: overview, names, and addresses

What 1NEON is, how its frame works, every kind of ID and name it shows, and the address of every page.

1NEON is neon1's client portal at neon1.tech/1NEON. Each client organization runs its projects there with neon1. Every project moves through four layers, N E O N: **Needs** (what's wanted, and the options to get there), **Execute** (the work), **Observe** (the results checked against the goals), and **Normalize** (handover, training, and care, so the change lasts). This guide describes every page, state, and action, so Neo can explain any of them, link to them, show them in a tour, and plan any action with a signed-in person.

## Who's who

- **neon1** is Pradeep's one-person business. In 1NEON, neon1 is the *operator*: it proposes options, does the work, and can enter every client organization. The operator role comes from sign-in configuration, never from data in the portal.
- **A client organization** (also called an organization, a client, or a tenant) is one business or household neon1 works with. Its people are invited by its admins or by neon1.
- **neon1's own organization** has the slug `neon1` and the client ID **N1-0001**. There neon1 is also the client, so neon1's people may approve options and name decision makers, which they can't do in any other organization.
- **A member** is a person in an organization, with one access level there: viewer, editor, or admin. One person can belong to several organizations with a different level in each.

## IDs and names people see

| Looks like | What it is | Where it shows |
|---|---|---|
| `N1-0001`, `N1-0002` | An organization's **client ID**, numbered in the order clients joined. N1-0001 is neon1 itself. Used in the organization chooser, on All clients, and on invoices. | Chooser, All clients, organization header |
| `acme-dental` | An organization's **slug**, its handle in addresses | `/1NEON/o/acme-dental/...` |
| `FLOW-1`, `MIG-2`, `HOME-1`, `PRJ-3` | A **project key**: a prefix from the project's template plus a number counted per organization and prefix | Cards, lists, the project page, search |
| `0039`, `0039-r2` | A **proposal number** and one of its **revisions**. Each project has one proposal; the first 1NEON issued is 0039, and each change is issued as the next revision | The proposal strip under Options, the proposal page, its PDF and Word copies |
| `0039-r2-B` | An **option ID**: the revision and the option's letter. A decision names the ID it approved | Options, decisions, purchases bought for an option |
| `INV-0039-01` | An **invoice number**: the proposal's number (or the project key when there's no proposal) and the invoice's place in the project. Set when neon1 issues it | Invoices, the invoice page, card statements (`NEON1* INV003901`) |
| Item titles | Items (requests, tasks, options, measures, and so on) are shown by title; their IDs only appear in links (`#item-…`) | Inside a project |

Project key prefixes come from the template chosen in New project: Blank is `PRJ`, Cloud migration is `MIG`, Workflow automation is `FLOW`, AI assistant is `AI`, Security readiness is `SEC`, and Personal or home tech is `HOME`. The number after the dash counts up per prefix within one organization, so `MIG-1` in two organizations are two different projects.

## The frame around every signed-in page

- **Menu** (top left; **Menu** at the bottom on phones) opens every page: Home, Board, Projects, Files, Insights, People, Settings, the four layers, and your profile. Choosing **Mini** on the profile also keeps a slim column of icons on the left.
- **Organization chooser** at the top of the menu switches between organizations a person belongs to. neon1 also sees **All clients** there.
- **Search** (the search button, Ctrl K or ⌘K, or `/`) jumps to any page or project and starts common actions: Start a new project and Upload a file for editors and admins, Invite people for admins.
- **?** (top right) opens help for the page in view: what it's for, a few how-tos, **Show me on this page** (a spotlight tour of that page), and **Full tour**.
- **The bell** glows when something new happened in the organization: a file upload, a decision, a stage move, a new comment, and similar. Opening it lists what changed and who did it.
- **Neo** sits at the bottom right: the assistant that answers questions, links to pages, runs tours, and, with the person's go-ahead, does things for them.
- **A read-only banner** shows on All clients: "read only. Open a client to make changes."

## Themes

A person picks a look on their profile: **Awake** (light, the default), **Matrix** (dark, green on black, like the landing page's rain), or **Device** (follows the device's light or dark setting). Neo's window follows the same look as the page around it.

## Addresses

Every signed-in page lives under `https://neon1.tech/1NEON/`. In the table, `{org}` is the organization's slug and `{KEY}` a project key.

| Page | Address |
|---|---|
| Sign-in | `/1NEON/` |
| Home (the organization's starting page) | `/1NEON/o/{org}/workspace` |
| Board | `/1NEON/o/{org}/workflow` |
| Projects (list and timeline) | `/1NEON/o/{org}/projects` |
| New project | `/1NEON/o/{org}/projects/new` |
| One project, Overview | `/1NEON/o/{org}/projects/{KEY}` |
| One project, a layer | `/1NEON/o/{org}/projects/{KEY}/needs`, `/execute`, `/observe`, or `/normalize` |
| Options on a project | `/1NEON/o/{org}/projects/{KEY}/needs#options` |
| The project's proposal | `/1NEON/o/{org}/projects/{KEY}/proposal` |
| A project's invoices | `/1NEON/o/{org}/projects/{KEY}/execute#billing` |
| One invoice | `/1NEON/o/{org}/projects/{KEY}/invoices/{invoiceId}` |
| The service agreement, to sign | `/1NEON/o/{org}/agreement` |
| Files asked for on a project | `/1NEON/o/{org}/projects/{KEY}/needs#files` |
| One item on a project | `/1NEON/o/{org}/projects/{KEY}/{layer}#item-{itemId}` |
| One layer across all projects | `/1NEON/o/{org}/layer/needs` (also `execute`, `observe`, `normalize`) |
| People | `/1NEON/o/{org}/people` |
| Files | `/1NEON/o/{org}/documents` |
| Insights | `/1NEON/o/{org}/insights` |
| Settings | `/1NEON/o/{org}/settings` |
| Your profile | `/1NEON/me` (two-step verification at `/1NEON/me#security`) |
| All clients (neon1 only) | `/1NEON/all/workflow` |
| FAQs, public | `/1NEON/faqs` |
| Sample project, public | `/1NEON/example` |
| Guided walkthrough, public | `/1NEON/live` (short ones: `?play=invite`, `passkey`, `authenticator`, `texts`, `start`, `needs`, `listen`, `propose`, `decide`, `build`, `observe`, `handover`, `care`, `team`, `profile`, `signin`) |
| Interactive demo, public | `/1NEON/demo/` |
| Privacy, terms, cookies, service agreement | `/1NEON/privacy`, `/1NEON/terms`, `/1NEON/cookies`, `/1NEON/agreement` |

The address word for Execute is `execute` and for Normalize is `normalize`. Older links that say `execution` or `next` still work.

## Spotlight anchors

Tours point at named spots on a page. Each name below exists only on the page listed, and only while that part is on screen.

| Anchor | Page | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `nav-home`, `nav-board`, `nav-projects`, `nav-layers`, `nav-files`, `nav-me` | Every page | Menu entries (the menu must be open, or Mini on) |
| `menu` | Every page | The menu button |
| `search` | Every page | The search button |
| `help` | Every page | The ? button |
| `notifications` | Organization pages | The bell |
| `needs-you`, `coming-up`, `get-started`, `activity` | Home | Needs you, Coming up, Get started, Recent activity |
| `board-column`, `board-card` | Board, All clients | A stage column, a project card |
| `new-project`, `project-list` | Projects | New project button, the list |
| `next-step`, `stage`, `layers` | One project | Next step box, the stage line, the layer tabs |
| `proposal` | One project, Needs | The proposal strip under Options: the revision, its price check, and Issue or Read the proposal |
| `wizard` | New project | The questions |
| `layer-list` | One layer across projects | The list |
| `invite`, `people-list` | People | Invite people, the list of people |
| `upload` | Files | The upload area |
| `kpis`, `weekly`, `by-layer` | Insights | The numbers on top, Finished per week, Projects by layer |
| `stages` | Settings | The stage rows |
| `passkey` | Profile | Two-step verification |
